articles.summary: - Company to Host Learning Theatre on aPAP with Renowned Key Opinion Leader Along with Members of the Patient Community - Savara Inc. (Nasdaq: SVRA), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on rare respiratory diseases, today announced the acceptance of an encore oral presentation on data from the Phase 3 IMPALA-2 clinical trial and a poster presentation on data from the Phase 2/3 IMPALA clinical trial at CHEST 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona, October 18–21. Oral Presentation Title: Long-Term Efficacy and Safety of Molgramostim in Patients with Autoimmune Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis (aPAP): Results From the IMPALA-2 Trial Open-Label Treatment Period Session ID: 4175, ILD Treatment Updates Date/Time: Tuesday, October 20, 2026, 1:45 – 2:30 PM MST Location: Phoenix Convention Center, Arizona (Exhibit Hall Rapid Fire Area 2D) Presenter: Bruce C. Trapnell, M.D., Professor of Medicine and Pediatrics, University of Cincinnati College of Medicine, Cincinnati, OH, U.S.
articles.title: Savara to Present New Analysis from the IMPALA Clinical Trial and Deliver Encore Presentation of Long-Term Data on Molgramostim in Autoimmune Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis (aPAP) at CHEST 2026

articles.summary: - Post-Hoc Analysis of the Phase 2/3 IMPALA Clinical Trial Presented in a Poster Presentation at the CHEST 2026 Annual Meeting - Savara Inc. (Nasdaq: SVRA) (the Company), a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on rare respiratory diseases, presented a poster at the CHEST 2026 Annual Meeting in Phoenix, Arizona. The poster reports a post-hoc analysis of the IMPALA clinical trial evaluating the effects of molgramostim in aPAP patients with mildly decreased or normal diffusion capacity, defined as a baseline percent predicted hemoglobin-adjusted diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide (DLco%) greater than 70%. Below is a summary of the data presented. Poster 4315: “Molgramostim Treatment Effects in Autoimmune Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis Patients with Mild Diffusion Impairment,” presented by B.C.
